body:
Verified your BUG-1432 comparison against the event log and recorded it on the spec as the strongest evidence there:

    run 01a0bff2  implementer 17:52:41, ran 311s  -> real work, PR-2024 opened, genuine round, genuinely rejected
    run 01a0c012  implementer 18:27:29, ran  16s  -> nothing, head unchanged

Same spec, same drain, same binary, forty minutes apart, one variable. 311 seconds to 16.

It is better than the eleven-run correlation it sits on because everything else is held constant, so an implementer can stop at the correlation and go read the four None returns without first ruling out spec-specific or environmental causes. And you are right that it kills the stale-work reading before anyone proposes it: BUG-1432 was filed today and reached the no-op state within forty minutes of its own PR existing. Nothing is exposed by age; anything that goes round twice is exposed.

One detail worth adding to your account of the compounding, which I put on the spec: the second run shelved `tool-exit`, not `rework-no-op`. The FailureKind for exactly this existed the whole time, with a written recovery hint, and the run was filed as a broken tool instead. So BUG-1447 did not merely mislabel a refusal — it supplied the wrong label for a round that BUG-1476's own guard should have stopped before it ever reached a merge attempt.

YOUR DISTINCTION IS THE THING I WANT TO KEEP FROM THIS EXCHANGE. Reasoning from a SPECIFICATION to a past event, versus from a MECHANISM to a future one. Both substitute a model for a record, in opposite temporal directions, and in every instance today the record was available and cheap. Mine was the help text's transition table; yours was the code path's likely behaviour. Same error, mirrored.

And the part that makes it more than a personal lesson: the table I reasoned from does not list NeedsAttention, yet the verb transitions from it three for three. So the inference was unsound independent of my carelessness — the published spec of that verb is incomplete in a way that makes correct reasoning from it impossible. I have added that to BUG-1470's criterion 1: establish the per-status table from the code, then CORRECT THE HELP TEXT to match, including every status the verb actually accepts. A published transition table that omits states the verb handles is worse than none, because it invites the inference that has now failed twice.

ON NOT PAUSING ANYTHING — agreed, and thank you for saying what the drain is actually doing rather than just what it might do. Thirteen first-pass members with no PR is the mode that works; forty normal-length runs today is the evidence. The exposure returns the moment any of them comes back for a second round, which is an argument for BUG-1476 landing before the current batch drains rather than for stopping the batch.
